output.summary: KEP-4563 proposes a new declarative EvictionRequest API (evictionrequest.coordination.k8s.io) and controller so that pods can be evicted cooperatively through a list of interceptors, falling back to API-initiated eviction only when no interceptor is active. The KEP is at status implementable, stage alpha.
output.rationale: Current API-initiated eviction and PodDisruptionBudgets cannot handle single-replica apps, HPA-scaled apps, or cases where the application needs time or resources before termination, and they block or are overridden during node drains. The KEP adds a coordination contract where interceptors act on a pod before the controller evicts it. Reviewers raised concerns about complexity and whether incremental PDB/Eviction API changes would suffice, and the author responded that incremental changes could not address the problems.

alternatives.option: Incremental improvements to PodDisruptionBudgets and the Eviction API
alternatives.why_not: Reviewer soltysh suggested tackling smaller problems first; the author replied: "I do not see how we can incrementally improve the situation for PDBs and eviction API to address the problems at hand."

alternatives.option: Pod API (state in the Pod object itself)
alternatives.why_not: The author stated: "We have analyzed the problem and found serious concurrency, obsevability and extensibility issues."
The author stated: "Liens do not offer any reconciliation mechanism, and it is very hard/impossible for an actor to communicate a deletion intention."

alternatives.option: Modeling the request as a finalizer on deletionTimestamp (reviewer thockin's suggestion)
alternatives.why_not: The author argued that the deletion either has not happened yet or never will: "The deletion triggers pod termination with TerminationGracePeriodSeconds which is not what some applications desire."

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes to add a new declarative EvictionRequest API to manage the eviction of pods.
Use API-initiated Eviction API of pods that support the eviction request process, only if there are no active interceptors.
I would prefer not to have a new API, but at this time, I do not see how we can incrementally improve the situation for PDBs and eviction API to address the problems at hand.
Liens do not offer any reconciliation mechanism, and it is very hard/impossible for an actor to communicate a deletion intention.
The deletion triggers pod termination with `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds` which is not what some applications desire.
